narrative_purpose: Show that a pursuit is decided by turn radius rather than speed: the faster four-winged pursuer overshoots wide while the slower prey cuts inside it on a tighter circle.
subject: Two large flying creatures locked in a tight spiral. The PURSUER is the big four-winged dark predator, banked hard but carried wide on a large sweeping arc, its nose pointing past its target rather than at it. The PREY is a smaller single-pair-winged flyer cutting inside on a visibly much tighter circle, already turning across the pursuer's path. Faint spiralling trails of disturbed hazy air mark both flight paths, the pursuer's arc obviously the larger of the two.
scene: Open air above dark basalt ridges with ash haze thinning at altitude, the ground far below indistinct.
camera: High oblique view looking down onto the plane of the turn, so both flight arcs and the difference in their radii are clearly visible.
light: Flat ashen daylight from above, a faint warm underglow from distant venting far below, cool teal bio-glow along the smaller flyer's wing edges.
palette: Charcoal and crimson on the pursuer, cooler teal-grey on the prey, indigo haze throughout, one restrained warm accent far below.
style: Painterly naturalist plate, tense and observed, no comic-book speed effects.
detail_level: Crisp on both animals; the air trails soft and semi-transparent; the ground fully hazed.
composition: Two nested arcs filling the frame, the wide arc sweeping through the outer edge and the tight arc inside it, plain hazy space in the lower third for overlaid callouts.
consistency_notes: The pursuer is the same four-winged animal as the cover, two separate driven wing pairs and a forward bone horn. The prey must be visibly smaller with only one wing pair. The pursuer's turn arc must be unmistakably wider than the prey's - that difference is the entire point of the figure.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no dotted trajectory lines, no comic speed lines, no green rainforest, no aircraft, no 3D-render or photographic look, no cartoon style
